welcome.title: A quick walk round with Pearl

lines.text: Hello, love. I can see you’re new here. I’m Pearl.
Let me show you round. I’ll do the pointing, you do the nodding.
Two minutes, and I’ll try not to go on. Shall we?
Today’s pick: {siteName}. {newCount} birds there you’ve not got yet.
lines.fallback: This card is today’s pick: the best spot for new birds within your drive.

lines.text: Someone saw {aBird} there {when}.
lines.fallback: It says what’s been seen there lately.

lines.text: It’s {minutes} minutes in the car. I’d take a flask.
lines.fallback: And how long the drive is. I’d take a flask.

lines.text: Tap any other pin and the card swaps over.
Thirty, sixty, ninety: how far you’ll drive. I get the bus, so I’m no judge.
After one bird in particular? Find a bird looks it up for you.
Saves squinting at eBird with your glasses on your head.
Go on, have a nose. Tap View spot.
Here’s what birders have seen there lately, each with a date.
Mind, those are other people’s birds. They don’t go in your Dex.
No pinching. I’d know.
This is your Dex. {recorded} of {dexSize} so far.
lines.fallback: This is your Dex: a hundred-odd birds you can find round here.

lines.text: Grey ones are still out there. I’ve left the names on, so no excuses.
Two ways to fill it: bring your eBird history in, or log a bird yourself.
Only birds you’ve seen or heard yourself. I’m fussy about that.
And this is Folk. Wardens at the reserves, and a few regulars.
Birders do need mates. Hours in a hide, not a word said.
Pop by their patch and they’ll remember you. Some will set you jobs.
When you log a new bird, I’ll draw it for you.
Fair warning: they all come out looking like this wren.
Off you go, then. I’m in Settings if you get lost. Bring me something good.
